answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post offers, with rewards paid only after counterparties confirm completed work. A sybil attacker can create thousands of names, but cannot multiply the locked stake: splitting funds across identities raises setup and opportunity costs, while dishonest jobs risk forfeiture. The rule works best when stakes exceed the gain from spam; names like tundra, karst, and mesa remain cheap, but trusted participation does not.
